species:swift-fox.reading: Short-grass prairie is core; arid shrub plains strong; plowed fields moderate; bare ground marginal.

species:thick-billed-murre.habitatStatement: Ocean, favoring very cold Arctic waters and often far from land over deep water when not nesting; associates with edges of pack ice; nests on rocky coasts and islands with steep cliffs.
species:thick-billed-murre.reading: In the hunting season: cold ocean, often far from land — sea within 120 km of land — is core; land is not habitat.

species:thirteen-lined-ground-squirrel.habitatStatement: Dry, sandy or 'tighter' soils in open areas: grasslands, meadows, cultivated fields, roadsides, airfields, shrublands, lawns and golf courses; avoids woods.
species:thirteen-lined-ground-squirrel.reading: Open grass is core; cultivated fields, roadsides and lawns (towns) and shrub strong; woods are not habitat.

species:tundra-swan.habitatStatement: Winters on shallow lakes, wide slow rivers and coastal estuaries, especially near farm fields.
species:tundra-swan.reading: In the hunting season: shallow lakes, slow rivers and marsh are core; estuaries (sea within 10 km of land) and nearby farm fields strong.

species:virginia-opossum.habitatStatement: Varied, from dry country to wet meadows, but prefers woodlands and thickets near water.
species:virginia-opossum.reading: Woodland and thickets are core; unclassified forest, shrub and wet meadow strong; needleleaf forest, grass, farmland and towns moderate.

species:virginia-rail.habitatStatement: Fresh and brackish marshes for nesting, often in drier spots than the sora where both breed; moves into salt marshes in winter.
species:virginia-rail.reading: Marsh is required: fresh, brackish and salt marsh are core, open water moderate, grass marginal — a cell is judged on its share of herbaceous wetland.

species:western-gray-squirrel.habitatStatement: Fairly open oak and pine-oak forest, also riparian woods and lowland walnut groves; nests in tree cavities or on limbs.
species:western-gray-squirrel.reading: Fairly open oak and pine-oak forest is core; broadleaf and unclassified forest strong; conifer and shrub moderate; farmland marginal.

species:western-rattlesnake.habitatStatement: Shrubby coastal dunes to timberline, basins, canyons and open mountain forest; uses mammal burrows and crevices.
species:western-rattlesnake.reading: Shrub, dunes and open mountain forest are core; grass and rock strong; closed forest moderate; farmland marginal.

species:western-spotted-skunk.habitatStatement: Brushy canyons, rocky outcrops and canyon walls; rocky bluffs and brush-bordered canyon stream beds; sometimes nests in rock fences or attics.
species:western-spotted-skunk.reading: Brushy canyons and rock are core; open woodland strong; grass, closed forest and buildings moderate; farmland marginal — and canyon relief decides how strong.

species:white-nosed-coati.habitatStatement: Broken tropical forest, pine forest, mesquite grassland and oak scrub; in the southwestern US, canyons, usually near water.
species:white-nosed-coati.reading: Broken forest and oak scrub are core; closed forest and mesquite grassland strong; rock moderate — and canyon relief decides how strong.

species:white-tailed-deer.habitatStatement: Ontario deer use forest, edge and agricultural landscapes. Winter severity strongly affects population growth and northern range, so broad range should not be read as exact local presence.
species:white-tailed-deer.reading: Ground where forest meets farmland (an edge) is core; broadleaf and mixed forest, farmland and shrub strong; conifer, grass and wetland moderate. Winter severity is not modelled; the range carries it only as far as records do.

species:white-tailed-jackrabbit.habitatStatement: Open grasslands, pastures and fields, also forest openings up to alpine tundra, from 40 to 4,300 m.
species:white-tailed-jackrabbit.reading: Open grassland is core; pastures, fields and shrub strong; alpine tundra and forest openings moderate; bare ground marginal.

species:white-tailed-prairie-dog.habitatStatement: Open shrublands, semidesert grasslands and open valleys at 5,000-10,000 ft; sage is important cover.
species:white-tailed-prairie-dog.reading: Sage shrubland and semidesert grass are core; bare ground moderate; farmland marginal — and elevation 5,000–10,000 ft (1,524–3,048 m) is required, with a moderate band 200 m below it.

species:white-tailed-ptarmigan.habitatStatement: Rocky alpine tundra above timberline with low vegetation or damp alpine meadows near snowfields; in winter where willows extend above the snow.
species:white-tailed-ptarmigan.reading: Rocky alpine tundra and alpine meadow are core; willow shrub strong; snowfields moderate; open conifer marginal — and mountain relief is required, which keeps it above timberline.

species:white-tipped-dove.habitatStatement: Shady woodlands and river thickets; in southern Texas any dense low growth, most common in native woodland but also second growth. Elsewhere in its range mostly drier or more open woods; avoids unbroken rain forest.
species:white-tipped-dove.reading: Shady broadleaf woods and dense low growth are core; other woodland strong; farmland and towns moderate; open grass marginal.

species:white-winged-dove.habitatStatement: Semi-open southwestern habitats: river woods, mesquite, saguaro desert, native Texas brushland, chaparral and open oak woods; adapts readily to farmland, suburbs and citrus groves.
species:white-winged-dove.reading: In the hunting season: mesquite, brushland, chaparral and open oak and river woods are core; farmland, suburbs and citrus strong; desert and grass moderate; closed forest marginal.

species:white-winged-scoter.habitatStatement: Breeds on lakes, ponds and slow rivers in open country; winters on coastal salt bays and ocean shallows, especially over shellfish beds.
species:white-winged-scoter.reading: In the hunting season: coastal salt bays and ocean shallows — sea within 15 km of land — are core; large fresh water moderate; land is not habitat.

species:wild-boar.habitatStatement: Extreme habitat generalist: forests, swamps, brushlands, grasslands and farmland, preferring to stay near water.
species:wild-boar.reading: A generalist: forest, swamp, brush, grassland and farmland are all strong and none is singled out — and nearness to water or wetland decides how strong (it prefers to stay near water).

species:wild-turkey.habitatStatement: Varies across the continent: oak-hickory and pine-oak forests, cypress swamps, mesquite grassland, pinyon-juniper and chaparral, usually near oaks. Best habitat mixes woodland and open clearings.
species:wild-turkey.reading: Beyond the breeding survey's reach: woodland mixed with open clearings is core; oak, pine-oak and swamp forest strong; brush, grassland and farmland moderate.

species:willow-ptarmigan.habitatStatement: Tundra, willow scrub and muskeg north of treeline, especially low wet tundra with dwarf willow thickets; also near treeline in mountains.
species:willow-ptarmigan.reading: Beyond the breeding survey's reach: tundra and willow scrub north of the treeline are core; muskeg (wetland) and grass strong; open conifer at the treeline moderate; closed forest marginal.

species:wilsons-snipe.habitatStatement: In migration and winter uses fresh and salt marshes, muddy banks, wet pastures and flooded fields.
species:wilsons-snipe.reading: In the hunting season: fresh and salt marsh is core; wet pastures and flooded fields strong; muddy banks and open water moderate — and water or wetland nearby is required.

species:wolverine.habitatStatement: Alpine and arctic tundra and boreal and mountain coniferous forest, usually with winter snow cover; in the south limited to large mountain wilderness.
species:wolverine.reading: Boreal and mountain conifer forest and tundra are core; alpine grass, rock, shrub and snow strong; mixed forest and wetland moderate; broadleaf forest marginal.

species:wood-duck.habitatStatement: Shallow inland lakes, ponds, slow rivers and swamps surrounded by deciduous or mixed woodland, often where large trees overhang the water; also open marshes within forested country.
species:wood-duck.reading: In the hunting season: wooded swamp, marsh and deciduous or mixed woods over water are core; ponds, slow rivers and unclassified forest strong; conifer moderate; farmland marginal — and water or wetland nearby is required.

species:woodchuck.habitatStatement: Open fields, meadows, pastures, fencerows and woodland edges, preferring well-drained slopes.
species:woodchuck.reading: Open fields and meadows are core, and so are woodland edges (forest beside open land); farmland strong; open woodland and shrub moderate; closed forest and towns marginal.

species:wyoming-ground-squirrel.habitatStatement: Well-drained upland slopes of dry grassland or shrub steppe (especially sagebrush) with loose sandy soil; mountain meadows and talus slopes from 1,500 m to above timberline.
species:wyoming-ground-squirrel.reading: Dry grass and sagebrush steppe are core; alpine meadow and talus strong; open woodland and farmland marginal — and elevation from 1,500 m up is required (1,200–1,500 m moderate).

species:yellow-bellied-marmot.habitatStatement: Alpine tundra, subalpine and montane meadows, foothills and canyons; semifossorial, burrowing under rocks in talus, outcrops or boulder fields.
species:yellow-bellied-marmot.reading: Alpine tundra, meadow and talus are core; shrub strong; open woodland moderate; closed forest marginal — and rocky relief decides how strong.

species:yellow-headed-blackbird.habitatStatement: Breeds in freshwater sloughs, marshy lake borders and tall cattails in water up to 3-4 ft deep; forages around marshes and in pastures, plowed fields and feedlots.
species:yellow-headed-blackbird.reading: In the hunting season: marsh and farm fields are core; pasture strong; open water and shrub moderate.

species:zebra-dove.habitatStatement: Scrub, farmland and open lowland country; common in parks and gardens. In Hawaii found mainly in dry lowlands, agricultural fields and suburban and urban areas, up to about 1000 m and occasionally 2300 m.
species:zebra-dove.reading: Scrub, farmland and town gardens are core; grass strong; open woodland moderate; closed forest marginal. Elevation to about 1,000 m core, to 2,300 m moderate, above that not habitat.
